wikilink chips carry data-wanted, so a link to an unwritten page is visibly wanted rather than an error; what a chip does on click is the workbench's decision, handed in

actions_taken: tests/integration/markdown-highlight.test.ts takes 'survives restart' literally: the database is closed and reopened from the same path between making the highlight and finding it again, so nothing under test is carried across in memory

the selection is derived the way MarkdownReaderView derives it -- offsets against the normalized document text, not the DOM -- and the anchor is built by the reader's own createMarkdownAnchorFromSelection

the load-bearing case is the edited file: a section inserted above the quote invalidates every stored offset, the re-import changes the contentHash, and resolution re-finds the quote by context instead
the third test is the one that keeps the second honest: when the sentence is deleted the anchor resolves to null rather than to a plausible wrong paragraph, and the annotation row is kept
errors: @wr/markdown-reader has no vitest alias and its entrypoint pulls in React; the anchoring module is imported by path instead, as the main-process modules in this suite already are

actions_taken: parseFileRequest replaces parseFileId internally and returns {fileId, resourcePath}; parseFileId is kept and still returns null for any path within a file, so the single-file callers cannot silently start accepting one
a resource is only served when the addressed row is text/html: a PDF row is not a handle on the directory it happens to share with other people's documents, which is how Zotero stores attachments

the resource is bounded twice -- lexically against the snapshot directory, then again after resolveAllowedPath follows symlinks -- because the allowed roots are the whole library and would happily serve a sibling item
blocksRemoteRequest is extracted from lockDownNavigation so the thing that stops archived markup phoning home is assertable without an Electron session
FileRequestServices narrows AppServices to db/allowed/logger so the rules are exercised against a real database and real files with no Zotero client standing by to satisfy a type
errors: the encoded-separator forms (..%2f..) are the ones that actually reach the handler: the URL parser collapses `..` and `%2e%2e` only when they stand as a whole segment, so the boundary cannot be enforced during parsing and is enforced against the resolved path instead
